0.comment: Jean: Barbara and the Gunnhildr family
0.content:
Jean's parents are Frederica Gunnhildr, the Alder Knight of the Gunnhildr Clan, and Seamus Pegg, a famed adventurer who became the Church of Favonius's Seneschal, the Cardinal of Daybreak. They separated when the girls were small. Jean stayed with her mother, who raised her strictly as heir to the clan, and Barbara went with their father into the Church. Jean has always wanted to be closer to her sister but cannot find the words before Barbara's evasive glances; Barbara is equally awkward, and secretly worries about her. When Jean collapsed from overwork, Barbara nursed her and told her friends that Jean goes to Vennessa's tree when she feels lost, then claimed Jean had "mentioned it".

Frederica, Varka's second-in-command on the expedition, mailed Jean a fine sword from the road. She was later sent back to defend Dornman Port and, with Barbara, surprised Jean at headquarters the evening before her 2025 birthday. Seamus returned after the Nod-Krai crisis and says Jean's temperament is "perhaps too much like her mother's". In 6.5 he told Varka that people need to force her to rest. On her 2026 birthday, Varka ordered her to take the day off, and she came home to find her father kneading pizza dough and Barbara chopping mint for a family dinner.

1.content:
Varka, the Knight of Boreas and Grand Master, left six months before the Traveler arrived with the Knights' elite, telling Jean, "you've basically been doing my job for years now, anyway." She once begged him to take his job seriously; he replied that helping him was part of a second-in-command's job. She does not resent him. He is "the knight of new frontiers", she "the knight of maintaining peace and freedom", and she vowed to show him a kinder, more prosperous Mondstadt on his return. She calls him the legend of his generation.

Before leaving, Varka privately told her that if he did not come back she must become Grand Master and train the next Knight of Boreas. She kept it secret until his return was imminent (6.4). Her letter to him ("Dear Grand Master...") was among those that guided him out of the Ley Lines. Varka believes she has more talent for the role than he does, and she always says she is not qualified. During the limited-time 6.4 homecoming event he turned up early at her festival's drink stall; flustered, she apologised for the preparations, then took him straight to headquarters to review documents before dawn.

2.content:
Jean is one of the few Mondstadters who know the bard Venti is Barbatos; she worked it out on her own. She keeps the secret absolutely, calls him Lord Barbatos only in private, and does not question an Archon's "own calculations". He agrees she is conscientious, courageous, kind and considerate, and says she reminds him of another good friend without saying whom.

After Signora tore out his Gnosis, Venti left the Cathedral without explanation. Jean understood where he had gone and went with the Traveler to the great tree at Windrise. In 5.6 she thanked him for his help in the city's defence, then named "Venti the bard" Windblume Star before the crowd; he asked if the title came with free drinks and swapped the acceptance speech for a song.

3.content:
After the Traveler helped drive off Stormterror and stabilise the elemental flow, Jean asked them to accept the title of Honorary Knight "and the gratitude of the Acting Grand Master". She has relied on them ever since, saying they have never failed Mondstadt in its time of need. She has sworn that, "not as the Acting Grand Master, but as Jean", her sword will always go with them.

She told them that when she walks with them "the path ahead becomes clearer", and that she can finally unwind in their company. When told she is beautiful when she smiles, she goes silent and suggests they walk while they talk. In 5.6 she involved them in Albedo's plan without telling them, and apologised afterwards. This is warm friendship and trust; canon does not make it a romance.

4.comment: Jean: Diluc and the Eroch affair
4.content:
Jean calls Diluc her senior and says they share the same commitment to protecting Mondstadt, though they have gone separate ways. He left the Knights after Inspector Eroch ordered him to cover up the death of his father, Crepus. Jean accepts his criticism ("I am not proud of the way things went, but I cannot change the past") and hopes her work will change his view. Diluc says trifling matters are her greatest enemy and that her sense of responsibility has kept her from her true calling. He still sponsored the party for her, saying he owes her his gratitude like any citizen.

Jean discovered Eroch's cover-up and reported it to Varka, who gave her authority to punish him. Eroch was discharged; she was promoted from squad captain to Master of the Knights, and with one hand held off Fatui diplomatic pressure while with the other she smashed the traitors' and the Abyss Order's plots. Her Vision came at that moment. In 6.4 Diluc revealed that before the expedition left, Varka had come to him over a drink, expressed regret about everything that happened and asked him to rejoin the Knights; Diluc declined, and his answer is unchanged.

5.comment: Jean: Vennessa, the Dandelion Knight and the Lionfang Knight
5.content:
Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius about a thousand years ago and ended her journey at Windrise, leaving a sapling that became the great tree. Jean reveres her. Jean says Vennessa was the Lionfang Knight when she overthrew the aristocracy and the Dandelion Knight when she founded the Knights, and that Masters of the Knights inherit one title or the other. After her collapse Jean prayed beneath the tree that Vennessa's watch over Mondstadt would remain unclouded, and later decided she is "definitely more of a Dandelion Knight": the Lionfang Knight stands for Vennessa's past battles, the Dandelion Knight for her hopes for the future.

Jean was granted the Dandelion Knight title at fifteen. That day she slipped away from the celebration to stand before the tree, doubting she was worthy, until the wind left her with one resolve: to become a warrior as kind and determined as Vennessa. She still goes there whenever she wavers. Some knights, like Hedwig, call her the Lionfang Knight; her constellation is Leo Minor, the lesser lion, and its sixth level is "Lion's Fang, Fair Protector of Mondstadt".

6.comment: Jean: Jean's collapse and the thank-you party
6.content:
In her story quest (1.0), the Traveler relays three requests to Jean: Sara's blocked supply road, Charles's tax forms and Margaret's missing cat Prince. Mid-report Jean stops responding and collapses from burnout; Barbara says it is not the first time. While she recovers, the Traveler takes over her commissions. She slips out to Windrise, where an Abyss Mage tries to kill her "in her moment of weakness", and despite coughing she insists on pursuing it. Back in the city, Swan lures her to Angel's Share, where the Knights, Barbara, Diluc and a very drunk Venti throw her a thank-you party; they have finished every task on her list. She is left speechless, then thanks everyone and slips up to the balcony.

Kaeya organised the party and gave the Traveler the credit to hide his own shyness; Lisa pushed the Traveler to find Jean "alone" upstairs. Asked if her work was done, Jean checked off the deliveries, the tax returns and finally Margaret's cat, to general despair.

7.content: During the Windblume season in 5.6, with Varka away, Jean convened all the captains and presided over a closed joint trial of Albedo for murder, with Dahlia as the Church's assessor. She found him guilty on the evidence. She told the captains it was as hard for her to accept as for anyone, and quietly set the Traveler to investigate. At the retrial an imposter Hertha was exposed and Durin's mimics attacked the city. The trial had been a trap planned for half a year: Jean had told Note that Hertha was away on a secret mission and had warned Barbara of coming attacks. She directed the defence, coordinated the knights over Venti's wind currents, and questioned the knight Phonia as she was exposed as being under Durin's influence. She later explained the Tripartite Conference between the Hexenzirkel, the Anemo Archon and the Knights and Church.

8.content: When Stormterror attacked, Jean already knew the dragon was Dvalin, one of the Four Winds. She asked the Traveler to clear the corrupted Ley Lines at the Temples of the Four Winds. She dismissed a Fatui envoy who wanted Mondstadt to kill the dragon, warning the Traveler that the Fatui covet the Anemo Archon's power. With the Fatui pressing and her official options few, she joined Diluc, Venti and the Traveler "as the normal Jean" to recover the stolen Holy Lyre. At Stormterror's Lair she thought killing Dvalin might be necessary until Venti explained the Traveler could purify him. Once he was saved, she told the people the truth about Dvalin.

9.content: When Lohen brought home Varka's letters in 6.4, the Traveler noticed something bothering Jean. She revealed Varka's contingency plan and explained the Knight of Boreas line. A wandering knight arrived with his wolf a thousand years ago and left no successor plan. His informal disciple Ravenwood saved the title, and since then it has passed down within the Knights, with the Knight of Boreas acting as intermediary with the Wolf of the North. She revealed that Boreas, or Andrius, came from Nod-Krai, a fact few even among the Knights know. She had kept this to herself rather than spread suspicion of the Four Winds after the Dvalin affair. She accepted that the true northern threat had been the Wild Hunt and the Doctor, and that preparing for every contingency is a leader's duty.

10.content: "Master Jean has a secret": despite the history books and the titles, she loves romance novels. It is not about the girlhood she lost to training, nor her parents' broken marriage. She simply longs for the kind of fragile mutual feeling those stories describe. Late at night in her office, finishing Vera's Melancholy, she wonders whether she might go to Cape Oath before daybreak if she has time. She keeps it entirely private; duty to Mondstadt and the Knights comes first. Canon gives her no partner.
